  • Method Details

    • enableUserRegistration

      @PostMapping("/enableUserRegistration") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity enableUserRegistration(@RequestBody com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode requestBody, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Enables user registration by adding an email address to the approved users list.

      This endpoint allows authenticated users to approve email addresses for registration. The requesting user must exist in the system and the email must have a valid format. If the email is already approved, the operation succeeds without duplicating the entry.

      Parameters:
      requestBody - JSON object containing:
      • username (string, required): username of the requesting user
      • email (string, required): email address to approve for registration
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP address logging and security monitoring
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with:
      • 200 OK: email successfully added to approved users list, body: "true"
      • 400 BAD REQUEST: missing required fields or invalid email format
      • 401 UNAUTHORIZED: username not found in system
      Example request body: 
      
 {
   "username": "admin_user",
   "email": "newuser@example.com"
 }
      All requests are logged with client IP address for security monitoring

    • getApprovedUsers

      @GetMapping("/getApprovedUsers") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity getApprovedUsers(@RequestHeader("username") String username, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Retrieves all email addresses that are approved for user registration.

      This endpoint returns a list of all email addresses that have been approved for registration in the system. Only authenticated users can access this information.

      Parameters:
      username - username of the requesting user (passed in HTTP header)
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP address logging
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with:
      • 200 OK: body contains JSON array of approved email addresses
      • 400 BAD REQUEST: missing or empty username header
      • 401 UNAUTHORIZED: username not found in system
      Response format: 
      
 ["user1@example.com", "user2@example.com", "user3@example.com"]

    • isEmailApproved

      @PostMapping("/isEmailApproved") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity isEmailApproved(@RequestBody com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode requestBody, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Checks whether an email address is approved for user registration.

      This endpoint verifies if a specific email address exists in the approved users list and can be used for account registration.

      Parameters:
      requestBody - JSON object containing:
      • email (string, required): email address to check
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP address logging
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with:
      • 200 OK: email is approved for registration, body: "ok"
      • 400 BAD REQUEST: missing email field in request body
      • 404 NOT FOUND: email is not in approved users list
      Example request body: 
      
 {
   "email": "user@example.com"
 }

    • addUser

      @PostMapping("/addUser") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity addUser(@RequestBody com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode requestBody, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Creates a new user account in the system.

      This endpoint allows the creation of new user accounts with specified roles. The user's password is automatically hashed using Argon2 before storage. Email validation is performed to ensure data integrity.

      Parameters:
      requestBody - JSON object containing:
      • user (object, required): user data object containing:
        • name (string, required): new user's username
        • email (string, required): new user's email address
        • password (string, required): new user's password (will be hashed)
        • role (integer, required): user role (0 = SUPERVISOR, other = WORKER)
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP address logging
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with:
      • 200 OK: user created successfully, body contains User object
      • 400 BAD REQUEST: missing required fields or invalid email format
      Example request body: 
      
 {
   "user": {
     "name": "john_doe",
     "email": "john@example.com",
     "password": "securePassword123",
     "role": 1
   }
 }
      Password is hashed using Argon2 algorithm before database storage
      See Also:
      • for role definitions

    • updateRoleUser

      @PostMapping("/updateRoleUser") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity updateRoleUser(@RequestBody com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode requestBody, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Updates the role of an existing user in the system. Only users with SUPERVISOR role can update other users' roles.
      Parameters:
      requestBody - JSON containing: - username: operator's username (must be SUPERVISOR) - user: object with target user data - email: target user's email (must be valid and exist) - role: new role as integer (0=SUPERVISOR, other=WORKER)
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP logging and security monitoring
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with: - 200 OK: role updated successfully, body contains updated User object - 400 BAD REQUEST: validation error, user not found, or insufficient permissions Exception handled generically with error message

      Example JSON request: { "username": "supervisor_user", "user": { "email": "target@example.com", "role": 1 } }

      Security notes: - All unauthorized attempts are logged with IP address - Only SUPERVISOR users can perform role updates - Target user is identified by email address

    • deleteUser

      @PostMapping("/deleteUser") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity deleteUser(@RequestBody com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode requestBody, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Deletes a user from the system.

      This endpoint allows authorized supervisors to delete user accounts from the system. Only users with SUPERVISOR role are permitted to perform this operation.

      Parameters:
      requestBody - JSON object containing the deletion request with the following required fields: - username: The username of the operator performing the deletion (must be a supervisor) - email: The email address of the user to be deleted (serves as the unique identifier)
      request - HTTP servlet request object used for logging the client's IP address
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity containing: - 200 OK with "true" if deletion is successful - 400 Bad Request if required fields (username/email) are missing from the request body - 401 Unauthorized if the operator does not have SUPERVISOR privileges - 404 Not Found if the operator username is not found in the system
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the user to be deleted does not exist (handled by repository layer)

      Security considerations: - Validates operator permissions before allowing deletion - Logs all deletion attempts with IP addresses for audit purposes - Logs unauthorized access attempts for security monitoring

      Usage example: POST /api/users/delete { "username": "supervisor_user", "email": "user.to.delete@example.com" }

    • authUser

      @PostMapping("/authUser") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity authUser(@RequestBody com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode requestBody, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Authenticates a user with email and password credentials.

      This endpoint verifies user credentials by checking the provided password against the stored Argon2 hash. Upon successful authentication, the user's password is cleared from the response object for security.

      Parameters:
      requestBody - JSON object containing:
      • email (string, required): user's email address
      • password (string, required): user's plaintext password
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP address logging
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with:
      • 200 OK: authentication successful, body contains User object (password cleared)
      • 400 BAD REQUEST: missing required fields (email or password)
      • 401 UNAUTHORIZED: invalid email or password
      Example request body: 
      
 {
   "email": "user@example.com",
   "password": "userPassword123"
 }
      All authentication attempts are logged with client IP address Password is cleared from response object for security

    • updatePassword

      @PostMapping("/updatePassword") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity updatePassword(@RequestBody com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode requestBody, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Updates a user's password after verifying their current password.

      This endpoint allows users to change their password by providing their current password for verification. The new password is hashed using Argon2 before storage. The operation is performed within a transaction to ensure data consistency.

      Parameters:
      requestBody - JSON object containing:
      • email (string, required): user's email address
      • oldPassword (string, required): current password for verification
      • newPassword (string, required): new password to set
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP address logging
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with:
      • 200 OK: password updated successfully, body: "true"
      • 400 BAD REQUEST: missing required fields
      • 401 UNAUTHORIZED: user not found
      • 403 FORBIDDEN: current password verification failed
      Example request body: 
      
 {
   "email": "user@example.com",
   "oldPassword": "currentPassword123",
   "newPassword": "newSecurePassword456"
 }
      Operation is transactional to ensure data consistency New password is hashed using Argon2 algorithm All password change attempts are logged with client IP address

    • getAllUsers

      @GetMapping("/getAllUsers") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity getAllUsers(@RequestHeader("username") String username, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Retrieves all user accounts from the system with sensitive information removed.

      This endpoint returns a list of all users in the system. Only users with SUPERVISOR role can access this information. For security, password fields are excluded from the response. The processing is optimized using parallel streams.

      Parameters:
      username - username of the requesting user (passed in HTTP header, must be SUPERVISOR)
      request - HttpServletRequest for IP address logging
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with:
      • 200 OK: body contains JSON array of User objects (without passwords)
      • 400 BAD REQUEST: missing username header
      • 401 UNAUTHORIZED: user not found or insufficient permissions
      Response format: 
      
 [
   {
     "username": "user1",
     "email": "user1@example.com",
     "role": "SUPERVISOR"
   },
   {
     "username": "user2",
     "email": "user2@example.com",
     "role": "WORKER"
   }
 ]
      Password fields are excluded from response for security Processing uses parallel streams for improved performance Only SUPERVISOR users can access this endpoint

    • ping1

      @GetMapping("/ping1") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Boolean> ping1()
      Health check endpoint to verify service availability.

      This endpoint provides a simple health check mechanism to verify that the authentication service is running and responding to requests. It always returns true and can be used for monitoring and load balancer health checks.

      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with 200 OK status and boolean true in body This endpoint does not require authentication Used for service health monitoring and load balancer checks
